MS George Eliot Review

Review of MS George Eliot

The 2019-built MS George Eliot cruise ship is currently operated under charter by the UK-based cruisetour company Riviera Travel on itineraries along the Danube, Rhine, and Moselle rivers, as well as Belgian and Dutch inland waterways. The riverboat is owned by the Swiss company Scylla AG.

The vessel George Eliot (ENI number 7002103) is currently Switzerland-flagged (MMSI 269057662) and registered in Basel.

IMPORTANT: In September 2025, Riviera Travel announced that starting in June 2027, the riverboat will be dedicated exclusively to solo travelers, offering double-occupancy cabins without single supplements.

Itineraries

For 2027, Riviera Travel scheduled four 7-night itineraries for George Eliot: "The Blue Danube River Cruise for Solo Travellers" (roundtrip from Budapest), "Rhine Cruise to Switzerland for Solo Travellers" (Cologne to Basel), "Rhine and Moselle River Cruise for Solo Travellers" (roundtrip from Cologne), and "Rhine, Strasbourg and Heidelberg for Solo Travellers" (roundtrip from Cologne).

The ship accommodates up to 68 solo travelers. A dedicated Cruise Director and Hotel Manager oversee onboard operations, while local guides lead daily shore excursions.

Shipboard Facilities and Amenities

The riverboat George Eliot features an elegant Lobby (entrance hall on Diamond/Upper Deck) with a Reception Desk (24-hour assistance, information, purser services), Travel Desk (for tour and excursion information and onboard cruise bookings), and a Boutique Shop. From the Lobby, passengers enter the Panorama Lounge (Bar Lounge) with floor-to-ceiling windows, comfortable seating, a full-service Bar, and the bow-located Lido Terrace offering small outdoor seating.

Aft on the Diamond Deck is the Bistro – Lido Restaurant, an alternative dining venue to the main Restaurant. The Bistro has its own Bar, doubles as a Library, and features an outdoor terrace and open kitchen. It serves early Breakfast, light Lunch, and Dinner. In fine weather, the floor-to-ceiling glass doors open fully onto the terrace for al fresco dining. Bistro dining is complimentary, though Dinner requires reservations due to limited capacity (10 tables for 2 or 4 guests). The main Dining Room Restaurant (on Ruby/Middle Deck) offers single-seating capacity with buffet-style Breakfast and waiter-served Lunch and Dinner.

On the Emerald/Lower Deck is the ship’s Wellness Centre, which includes a Beauty Salon (hairdresser, barber, and nail studio), Fitness Room (Gym), and Spa (massage treatment room). All cabin decks are fully air-conditioned and accessible via elevator (passenger lift) and stairs (forward, midship, and aft), including a grand staircase in the Atrium.

The Sun Deck features a leisure area with a Giant Chess Set, Mini-Golf Putting Green, shaded seating (under retractable awnings), a Walking Track, and an aft Pool Deck with Splash Pool, Jacuzzi/Whirlpool, and sunbathing area with loungers and deckchairs. The forward Alfresco Lounge offers full bar service from the Panorama Lounge on the Upper Deck. The forward-located Navigation Bridge (called “Wheelhouse” on riverboats) is passenger-accessible and telescopic, allowing it to lower when passing under low bridges.

Decks and Cabins

MS George Eliot has a total of 74 staterooms accommodating up to 148 passengers. Most cabins (83%) feature wall-to-wall and floor-to-ceiling glass doors opening to a railing (French Balcony). The only exceptions are the Emerald Deck cabins, which have one fixed, non-opening quarter-height window located near the ceiling.

All staterooms include hotel-style twin beds (convertible to double), en-suite bathroom (WC, shower, single-sink vanity, towels, bath toiletries, large mirror), 40-inch HDTV (satellite reception, infotainment system, bow camera views), mini-bar, tea/coffee-making facilities, glass-top round table with two armchairs, mirrored dressing table with pouf chair, wardrobe, electronic safe, hairdryer, telephone, individually controlled air conditioning, and evening turndown service.

All bathrooms feature marble countertops, glass showers (with large rain shower heads), and luxury bath products by Crabtree & Evelyn. Some staterooms are available for single occupancy bookings (without a single supplement, subject to availability). Deluxe Suites (on Diamond Deck) offer additional amenities, including larger interior space, a step-out balcony (furnished with a table and two chairs for al fresco dining), and premium cotton bathrobes and slippers.

The vessel has four decks, three of which are dedicated to passenger cabins.

MS George Eliot Wiki

The vessel’s construction (hull and superstructure, ENI number 07002103) was carried out at the Vahali Shipyard in Zasavica (Sremska Mitrovica, Serbia). The Dutch shipbuilding company Scheepswerf en Machinefabriek Vahali BV, founded in 1923, owns and operates shipyards in Serbia (Belgrade and Zasavica) and in the Netherlands (Gendt). Vahali Shipyard Zasavica officially opened in 2013. After the hull construction in Serbia, the cruise ship was towed to the Netherlands for final outfitting at Scheepswerf Vahali in Gendt.
